findings.title: js-yaml 4.3.1 — high-severity DoS (GHSA-2883-xcg3-v3hh)
findings.detail: js-yaml >=4.0.0 <4.3.2 does not limit CPU use for empty YAML merge sources, enabling a remote attacker to cause denial-of-service (CWE-400/407, CVSS 7.5). Installed version 4.3.1 is a transitive dev dependency via node_modules/@eslint/eslintrc. A fix is available (upgrade to >=4.3.2).
findings.suggested_fix: Run `npm audit fix` to update the package-lock.json entry for js-yaml to >=4.3.2

findings.title: Draft PR could not be created — PAT lacks GraphQL write scope
findings.detail: Branch claude-maintenance/2026-09-11-fix-js-yaml-cve was pushed successfully and contains the js-yaml 4.3.1→4.3.2 fix (all 89 tests pass, lint clean, build clean). However `gh pr create` failed: 'Resource not accessible by personal access token' — the GH_TOKEN used by the gh CLI does not have the `pull_requests: write` scope required by the GraphQL createPullRequest mutation. A human can open the PR manually from the pushed branch.
findings.suggested_fix: Grant the workflow token `pull_requests: write` permission, or manually open a PR from branch claude-maintenance/2026-09-11-fix-js-yaml-cve

findings.title: react / react-dom pinned to v18.3.1; latest is v19.3.0 (major bump)
findings.detail: package.json declares `react` and `react-dom` at ^18.3.1 (resolved to 18.3.1). The latest release is 19.3.0, one major version ahead. React 19 has breaking changes; this is flagged for awareness, not automated upgrade.
findings.suggested_fix: Manually evaluate React 19 migration guide and update package.json + code to ^19.3.0 when ready
